# Command-line reference

<!-- Generated by `epm2mod generate` from the command definitions. Do not edit. -->

Run a command with `uv run epm2mod COMMAND` in a checkout, or with the launcher in the release folder. `epm2mod COMMAND --help` shows the same text.

## Rules

- `--project DIR`, before the command, names the project folder: the folder of its `epm2mod.json`. Without it, the project is the nearest folder at or above the current folder that holds one. With none, a command exits 6.
- `--card DIR` is the top folder of an SD card. `-o FILE` is always a file, and never a file on an SD card that `epm2mod cards` lists (use `--card`).
- Results go to stdout. Progress, hints and the camera steps go to stderr.
- `--json` prints one document on stdout, on success and on failure (usage errors included). A file whose sha256 on the card is already right is not written again (`unchanged`).
- `--dry-run` prints what would be written and replaced, and writes nothing.
- No command asks a question. A refusal names the flag that overrides it (`--allow-untested`).
- `--film ARTn=FILM` puts one film simulation in one ART slot: ART1 to ART12, as in the camera's ART menu (ART1 Pop Art ... ART12 Watercolor). A slot named twice is an error. A slot that is not named keeps its Olympus art filter. With no `--film`, `install` writes the firmware only.
- In the release folder, the launcher's name takes the place of `epm2mod` in usage lines, examples and hints, and `--help` lists the commands for camera owners only.

| Exit status | Means | What a caller does |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | done (also: an empty cards list) |  |
| 1 | a check found a difference or a problem (generate --check, inspect "will not work", release not ready) | show it; like diff and grep |
| 2 | wrong usage | fix the command |
| 3 | not found: no such path, file not recognised, unknown build | fix the name or path |
| 4 | refused; a named flag overrides it (--allow-untested) | ask the user, then pass the flag |
| 5 | not safe: a checksum, read-back or download sha256 differs, firmware for another model | stop; never retry with a flag |
| 6 | environment: no network, no checkout, the card is not a camera card, not writable or full | fix the setup, then retry |
| 7 | failed: an input is wrong (a build description, a patch spec, a fit, a file that does not fit) | fix the input |
| 70 | internal error (an uncaught exception) | report |
| 130 | interrupted (any signal); no file half-written |  |

## JSON documents

Every `--json` document has these keys (`schema` 2). An added key does not change `schema`; a removed or renamed key, or a changed type, does. Ignore the keys you do not know. `a[].b` is the key `b` of each item of the list `a`; `a.b` is the key `b` of the object `a`.

- `schema`: the version of the document: 2
- `command`: the command, like films set (null for a usage error before the command is known)
- `version`: the tool's version
- `ok`: true if the command did its work (exit status 0)
- `error`: only on failure: what went wrong
- `error.code`: a stable name of the kind of failure
- `error.exit`: the exit status
- `error.message`: the message, as on stderr
- `error.override`: the flag that overrides a refusal (exit status 4), else null

## For camera owners

These commands work from the release folder, no checkout.

### epm2mod cards

List the SD cards in this computer.

```
epm2mod cards [-h] [--json]
```

- Output: a line per card: its name, size, free space and folder.
- Needs: no checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `cards`: the cards
- `cards[].path`: the top folder of the card
- `cards[].name`: the card's name
- `cards[].size`: its size in bytes
- `cards[].free`: its free space in bytes
- `cards[].label`: the line that the text output shows

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod cards
```

### epm2mod install

Write EPM2Mod to the SD card, and the look pack if --film is given.

```
epm2mod install [-h] --card DIR [--film ARTn=FILM] [--build BUILD] [--allow-untested] [--cache DIR] [--stock FILE] [--dry-run] [--eject] [--json]
```

- Output: the firmware on the card, and the look pack if --film is given; then the camera steps.
- Needs: no checkout. Network: when Olympus's firmware is not downloaded yet.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--card DIR` | the top folder of the SD card |  |
| `--film ARTn=FILM` | a film simulation for an ART slot: ART1 (Pop Art) to ART12 (Watercolor), names from 'epm2mod films'. Give it once per slot. The slots that are not named keep their Olympus art filter |  |
| `--build BUILD` | the name of another build; default: the pinned build |  |
| `--allow-untested` | allow a build that has no passed camera test |  |
| `--cache DIR` | the folder that keeps Olympus's firmware; default: the project's cache folder |  |
| `--stock FILE` | use this copy of Olympus's firmware (checked by its sha256); download nothing |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written and replaced; write nothing |  |
| `--eject` | eject the card after the write |  |
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `dry_run`: true if nothing was written
- `card`: the card, or null
- `build`: the build
- `build.name`: its name
- `build.what`: what it gives the user
- `build.sha256`: the sha256 of its firmware (null if it is not camera-tested)
- `build.tested`: true if it passed a camera test
- `build.camera_tested`: the date of that test, or null
- `build.label`: the label on the camera's Firmware screen, or null
- `files`: each file written, or with --dry-run to be written
- `files[].path`: where it goes
- `files[].role`: firmware or films
- `files[].size`: its size in bytes
- `files[].sha256`: its sha256 (null for a dry run of a build that is not camera-tested)
- `files[].replaced`: true if a different file of that name was there and is replaced
- `files[].unchanged`: true if that file already held these bytes: it was not written again
- `removed`: the extra files removed from DCOLYMP
- `films`: the films of the look pack
- `films[].art`: the ART slot, 1 to 12
- `films[].name`: the name the camera shows
- `ejected`: true if the card was ejected
- `eject_error`: why the card was not ejected after --eject (the files are written), else null
- `camera_steps`: the steps on the camera
- `camera_steps[].id`: what the step does, for a program (eject, flash, load-films, ...)
- `camera_steps[].text`: what the user reads

- Exit 3: no build of that name.
- Exit 4: a build without a passed camera test, without --allow-untested.
- Exit 5: a read-back or the sha256 of the result differs, or the firmware is for another model.
- Exit 6: no network, or the card is not a camera card, not writable or full.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod install --card /path/to/card
epm2mod install --card /path/to/card --film ART1=portra-400 --film ART2=velvia
```

### epm2mod films

List the film simulations and the 12 ART slots.

```
epm2mod films [-h] [--json] [ACTION] ...
```

- Output: a line per film: menu name, command-line name, film, type; then a line per ART slot with its Olympus art filter.
- Needs: no checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `films`: the films
- `films[].id`: the command-line name
- `films[].name`: the menu name
- `films[].film`: the film
- `films[].kind`: the type
- `films[].medium`: how the film was simulated
- `films[].note`: a remark, or an empty text
- `slots`: the 12 ART slots
- `slots[].art`: the slot, 1 to 12
- `slots[].entry`: its Olympus art filter

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod films
```

### epm2mod films set

Write only the look pack.

```
epm2mod films set [-h] (--card DIR | -o FILE) --film ARTn=FILM [--dry-run] [--eject] [--json]
```

- Output: the look pack on the card or at FILE; then the camera steps.
- Needs: no checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--card DIR` | the top folder of the SD card |  |
| `-o, --out FILE` | the file to write; not on an SD card (use --card) |  |
| `--film ARTn=FILM` | a film simulation for an ART slot: ART1 (Pop Art) to ART12 (Watercolor), names from 'epm2mod films'. Give it once per slot. The slots that are not named keep their Olympus art filter |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written and replaced; write nothing |  |
| `--eject` | eject the card after the write |  |
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `dry_run`: true if nothing was written
- `card`: the card, or null
- `files`: each file written, or with --dry-run to be written
- `files[].path`: where it goes
- `files[].role`: firmware or films
- `files[].size`: its size in bytes
- `files[].sha256`: its sha256 (null for a dry run of a build that is not camera-tested)
- `files[].replaced`: true if a different file of that name was there and is replaced
- `files[].unchanged`: true if that file already held these bytes: it was not written again
- `films`: the films of the look pack
- `films[].art`: the ART slot, 1 to 12
- `films[].name`: the name the camera shows
- `ejected`: true if the card was ejected
- `eject_error`: why the card was not ejected after --eject (the files are written), else null
- `camera_steps`: the steps on the camera
- `camera_steps[].id`: what the step does, for a program (eject, flash, load-films, ...)
- `camera_steps[].text`: what the user reads

- Exit 6: the card is not a camera card, not writable or full.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod films set --card /path/to/card --film ART2=velvia --film ART6=double-x
epm2mod films set -o EPM2LOOK.BIN --film ART1=portra-400
```

### epm2mod restore

Write Olympus's original firmware, to remove EPM2Mod.

```
epm2mod restore [-h] (--card DIR | -o FILE) [--cache DIR] [--stock FILE] [--dry-run] [--eject] [--json]
```

- Output: the original firmware on the card or at FILE; then the camera steps.
- Needs: no checkout. Network: when Olympus's firmware is not downloaded yet.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--card DIR` | the top folder of the SD card |  |
| `-o, --out FILE` | the file to write; not on an SD card (use --card) |  |
| `--cache DIR` | the folder that keeps Olympus's firmware; default: the project's cache folder |  |
| `--stock FILE` | use this copy of Olympus's firmware (checked by its sha256); download nothing |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written and replaced; write nothing |  |
| `--eject` | eject the card after the write |  |
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `dry_run`: true if nothing was written
- `card`: the card, or null
- `files`: each file written, or with --dry-run to be written
- `files[].path`: where it goes
- `files[].role`: firmware or films
- `files[].size`: its size in bytes
- `files[].sha256`: its sha256 (null for a dry run of a build that is not camera-tested)
- `files[].replaced`: true if a different file of that name was there and is replaced
- `files[].unchanged`: true if that file already held these bytes: it was not written again
- `removed`: the extra files removed from DCOLYMP
- `ejected`: true if the card was ejected
- `eject_error`: why the card was not ejected after --eject (the files are written), else null
- `camera_steps`: the steps on the camera
- `camera_steps[].id`: what the step does, for a program (eject, flash, load-films, ...)
- `camera_steps[].text`: what the user reads

- Exit 5: the download or a read-back differs.
- Exit 6: no network, or a card problem.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod restore --card /path/to/card
epm2mod restore -o E1019999.BIN
```

### epm2mod inspect

Say what a firmware file, a look pack or an SD card holds.

```
epm2mod inspect [-h] [--card DIR] [--json] [FILE]
```

- Output: a report per file (model, build, version, sha256, films) and what will not work.
- Needs: no checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `FILE` | a firmware file or a look pack |  |
| `--card DIR` | the top folder of the SD card |  |
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `card`: the card, or null
- `files`: a report per file
- `files[].path`: the file
- `files[].kind`: firmware or films
- `files[].size`: its size in bytes
- `files[].sha256`: its sha256
- `files[].model`: the camera model of a firmware file, else null
- `files[].build`: the build a firmware file is (a build name, or Olympus original), or null
- `files[].version`: the firmware's version, or null
- `files[].checksums_ok`: for a firmware file, true if every block's checksum is right, else null
- `files[].films`: the films of a look pack
- `files[].films[].art`: the ART slot
- `files[].films[].name`: the name the camera shows
- `files[].films[].kind`: colour or black-and-white
- `files[].problem`: what is wrong with the file, or null
- `problems`: what will not work, in words

- Exit 1: something will not work (see problems).
- Exit 3: no such file, a file it does not know, or a card with neither file.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod inspect --card /path/to/card
epm2mod inspect E1019999.BIN
```

### epm2mod serve

Open the installer page in the browser.

```
epm2mod serve [-h] [--port PORT] [--no-browser]
```

- Output: the page's address; the page writes the card.
- Needs: no checkout. Network: when Olympus's firmware is not downloaded yet.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--port PORT` | the port on 127.0.0.1; default: a free one |  |
| `--no-browser` | print the page's address in place of opening the browser |  |

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod serve
epm2mod serve --no-browser --port 8765
```

## For developers

These commands need a checkout.

### epm2mod make

Make a build into the output folder.

```
epm2mod make [-h] [-o FILE] [--out-dir DIR] [--cache DIR] [--stock FILE] [--dry-run] [--json] BUILD
```

- Output: NAME.BIN, and DCOLYMP with the firmware as on the card, in the output folder.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: when Olympus's firmware is not downloaded yet.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `BUILD` | the name of a build |  |
| `-o, --out FILE` | also write the firmware to FILE; not on an SD card |  |
| `--out-dir DIR` | the output folder; default: the project's output folder |  |
| `--cache DIR` | the folder that keeps Olympus's firmware; default: the project's cache folder |  |
| `--stock FILE` | use this copy of Olympus's firmware (checked by its sha256); download nothing |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written and replaced; write nothing |  |
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `dry_run`: true if nothing was written
- `build`: the build
- `build.name`: its name
- `build.what`: what it gives the user
- `build.sha256`: the sha256 of its firmware (null if it is not camera-tested)
- `build.tested`: true if it passed a camera test
- `build.camera_tested`: the date of that test, or null
- `build.label`: the label on the camera's Firmware screen, or null
- `sha256`: the firmware's sha256 (null for a dry run of a candidate)
- `files`: each file written, or with --dry-run to be written
- `files[].path`: where it goes
- `files[].role`: firmware or films
- `files[].size`: its size in bytes
- `files[].sha256`: its sha256 (null for a dry run of a build that is not camera-tested)
- `files[].replaced`: true if a different file of that name was there and is replaced
- `files[].unchanged`: true if that file already held these bytes: it was not written again

- Exit 3: no build of that name.
- Exit 5: the result is not the recorded build.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod make epm2mod-2026.11.19
epm2mod make debug-log -o E1019999.BIN
```

### epm2mod builds

List the build descriptions and the pinned one.

```
epm2mod builds [-h] [--json]
```

- Output: a line per build.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `pinned`: the name of the pinned build
- `builds`: the builds
- `builds[].name`: its name
- `builds[].what`: what it gives the user
- `builds[].sha256`: the sha256 of its firmware (null if it is not camera-tested)
- `builds[].tested`: true if it passed a camera test
- `builds[].camera_tested`: the date of that test, or null
- `builds[].label`: the label on the camera's Firmware screen, or null
- `builds[].specs`: the number of its patch specs

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod builds
```

### epm2mod init

Set up a checkout: the MN103 binutils, Node, the emulator, Olympus's firmware, the firmware map, the commit hooks.

```
epm2mod init [-h] [--check]
```

- Output: a line per item; with --check, what is present and what is missing, and nothing is changed.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: for what is missing: Olympus's firmware, the git submodules, a Node version through nvm.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--check` | change nothing; say what is present and what is missing, and exit 1 if an item is missing |  |

- Exit 1: with --check: an item is missing.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod init
epm2mod init --check
```

### epm2mod lint

Print what in a build may be harmful and is not proven safe.

```
epm2mod lint [-h] BUILD
```

- Output: WARN lines: jumps from early-loaded to late-loaded code, first code. Warnings do not change the exit status.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `BUILD` | the name of a build |  |

- Exit 6: the report cannot be made (Olympus's firmware or the MN103 objdump is missing).

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod lint NAME
```

### epm2mod pin

Record a passed camera test and pin the build.

```
epm2mod pin [-h] --date YYYY-MM-DD --sha256 HEX [--no-pin] [--dry-run] BUILD
```

- Output: the build description with the test record, and the pointer to the pinned build.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `BUILD` | the name of the tested build |  |
| `--date YYYY-MM-DD` | the day of the camera test |  |
| `--sha256 HEX` | the sha256 of the flashed file, from the camera log |  |
| `--no-pin` | record the camera test; leave the pinned build as it is |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written and replaced; write nothing |  |

- Exit 5: the build does not give that sha256.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod pin NAME --date 2026-11-19 --sha256 HEX
```

### epm2mod apply

Apply patch specs without a build description.

```
epm2mod apply [-h] -o FILE --from FILE [-v] [--cache DIR] [--stock FILE] [--dry-run] SPEC [SPEC ...]
```

- Output: the firmware file at FILE.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `SPEC` | patch spec files, in order |  |
| `-o, --out FILE` | the firmware file to write; not on an SD card |  |
| `--from FILE` | the firmware to start from |  |
| `-v, --verbose` | print each change |  |
| `--cache DIR` | the folder that keeps Olympus's firmware; default: the project's cache folder |  |
| `--stock FILE` | use this copy of Olympus's firmware (checked by its sha256); download nothing |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written and replaced; write nothing |  |

- Exit 3: the --from file is missing.
- Exit 5: the result is not the sha256 the spec states.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod apply SPEC --from OLY_E_101_1600_0000_0000.BIN -o test.BIN
```

### epm2mod fetch-stock

Download Olympus's firmware of the pinned build and check it.

```
epm2mod fetch-stock [-h] [--cache DIR] [--stock FILE] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

- Output: the firmware in the cache folder, and its path.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: when Olympus's firmware is not downloaded yet.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--cache DIR` | the folder that keeps Olympus's firmware; default: the project's cache folder |  |
| `--stock FILE` | use this copy of Olympus's firmware (checked by its sha256); download nothing |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written and replaced; write nothing |  |
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `path`: where the file is kept
- `sha256`: its sha256
- `downloaded`: true if it was downloaded now
- `dry_run`: true if nothing was downloaded

- Exit 5: the download is not the right file.
- Exit 6: no network.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod fetch-stock
```

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod films pack LIST --card /path/to/card
```

### epm2mod generate

```
epm2mod generate [-h] [--check]
```

- Output: the files it wrote; with --check, the files that differ.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|

### epm2mod log

Decode a camera log file (EPM2LOG.BIN).

```
epm2mod log [-h] [--dict FILE] [--json] FILE
```

- Output: a short report.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `FILE` | the log file from the SD card |  |
| `--dict FILE` | the event dictionary; default: the current one, and those of older builds |  |
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `events`: the events in order, each an object with the keys that the event dictionary gives it

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod log EPM2LOG.BIN
epm2mod log EPM2LOG.BIN --json
```

## For releases

These commands need a checkout.

### epm2mod package

Write the release zip.

```
epm2mod package [-h] [--out-dir DIR] --release-version V [--dry-run] [--json]
```

- Output: EPM2Mod-VERSION.zip in the output folder.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: never.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--out-dir DIR` | the folder for the zip; default: the output folder |  |
| `--release-version V` | the calendar version, like 2026.11.18 or 2026.11.18-rc.1; 2026.11.18-NAME.1 holds the build NAME in place of the pinned one |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written and replaced; write nothing |  |
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `dry_run`: true if nothing was written
- `zip`: the zip's path
- `sha256`: the zip's sha256 (null for a dry run)
- `firmware_sha256`: the sha256 of the firmware that the zip installs
- `contents`: the files in the zip

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod package --release-version 2026.11.19-dev
```

### epm2mod release

Check that the repository is ready for the next release, and name it.

```
epm2mod release [-h] [--final] [--build NAME] [--summary TEXT] [--json]
```

- Output: the release notes and the tag's name. It creates no tag: the release workflow on GitHub runs this command, then makes, tests, tags and publishes the release.
- Needs: a checkout. Network: the network, for the tags and main of origin.

| Argument | What | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--final` | a release for everyone (vYYYY.MM.DD); default: a test release (-rc.N) |  |
| `--build NAME` | a test release of this camera-tested build in place of the pinned one (-NAME.N) |  |
| `--summary TEXT` | what is new in this release, in plain sentences for users; the notes show it under the title |  |
| `--json` | print one JSON document (schema 2) on stdout |  |

`--json` keys beside the keys of every document:

- `ready`: true if the release can be made
- `problems`: why not, if it cannot
- `tag`: the tag of the release, like v2026.11.19-rc.1 (null if not ready)
- `release_version`: the release's version: the tag without its v (null if not ready)
- `title`: the title of the release page, like EPM2Mod 2026.11.19-rc.1 (null if not ready)
- `prerelease`: true for a test release, false for a release for everyone (null if not ready)
- `commit`: the commit that the release is made from (null if not ready)
- `notes`: the release notes (null if not ready)
- `sha256`: the sha256 of the firmware that the release installs (null if not ready)

- Exit 1: the repository is not ready for a release.

Examples:

```sh
epm2mod release
epm2mod release --final
epm2mod release --build NAME
```
